rv.q: The simulated instrumentation is extraordinary: not only do the performers recreate booming bass lines and pounding kick drums, they also mimic-pluck violins and jazzy, brushed-snare shuffles.
They consistently land some of the evening’s biggest laughs while never allowing the character to become a mere comic novelty. At the heart of the production is Amber Sylvia Edwards’ superb Wendy.

A delightful alternative to a Christmas pantomime. This Christmas season there will be two productions of Peter Pan flying into Wimbledon. Both will feature Peter, the Lost Boys and the dastardly Captain Hook, but will the New Wimbledon Theatre panto feature a bed that turns into a crocodile like this delightful production at Polka Theatre does?

Comedy comes from the pairing of Captain Hook (played with dandyish swagger to great effect by Hannah McPake) and the kindly boatswain Smee (Susannah van den Berg). Their bickering provides several laugh-out-loud moments, and a particularly delightful piece of shared comic choreography (credit to Sarah Golding) is a joy.

Second in popularity only to A Christmas Carol, what could be more festive than a new retelling of J. M. Barrie’s classic children’s tale, Peter Pan? Well, that’s what the Birmingham Rep theatre has gone for this season.

While musical versions of Peter Pan already exist, this new score is a pleasant refresh. The song Goodbye Make Believe is particularly beautiful, with a moving performance that makes it one of the show's standout scenes.
Ultimately, this Peter Pan is more successful at reinventing how Neverland sounds than at communicating the story that unfolds within it.

cn.t: Critics are largely won over by this hip-hop, beatbox reimagining of Barrie's classic at Polka Theatre. The all-vocal live soundscape earns particular praise, though execution is uneven.
